answer: Each identity holds a yarrow file of completed tasks funded from one key. Each epoch a falcon patrol samples 10% at random and replays each file, checking timestamps, outputs, and funding. A pass releases its nectar, the reward share; a fail burns its 45-credit bond. The k-th fake needs a fresh yarrow file at 45 credits, so cost grows linearly: a copied file carries the original funding key, so the cross-check rejects it. A rented history fails, since the renter lacks the funding key. One thousand fakes cost 45,000 credits; an honest agent pays 45 once.
